findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1917 is 'Cisco Nexus 9k Add-on for Splunk Enterprise (deprecated)', built by Cisco, and its listing tells users to migrate to the Cisco DC Networking app (7777). It is not called 'Splunk Add-on for Cisco Nexus' / Splunk_TA_cisco-nexus. The implementation and detailedImplementation sections still tell readers to install it on forwarders and search heads.
findings.suggested_fix: Make cisco_dc_networking_app_for_splunk (Splunkbase 7777) the primary collection app for Nexus 9000 NX-API data. Mention 1917 only as a deprecated legacy add-on, under its real Splunkbase name, or drop it. Apply the same fix in dataSources, implementation and detailedImplementation.

findings.explanation: Nexus 9000 CoPP best-practice profiles are strict, moderate, lenient and dense, so there is no 'default' profile to diff against. On Nexus 9000 the policy is named copp-system-p-policy-<profile> and the classes are copp-system-p-class-* (for example copp-system-p-class-critical). The UC uses copp-system-policy-strict/default/moderate and copp-system-class-critical/important/..., which are the Nexus 7000-style names, throughout detailedImplementation, visualization and the runbook.
findings.quote: run `**show copp diff profile strict profile default**` when debating `strict` versus `default` thresholds
findings.suggested_fix: Use `show copp diff profile strict profile moderate` (or lenient/dense) as the example. Change policy names to copp-system-p-policy-strict|moderate|lenient|dense and class names to copp-system-p-class-critical, -important, -normal, -redirect, -exception, -monitoring, -undesirable, -l3uc-data and so on, as listed in the Nexus 9000 CoPP configuration guide.

findings.explanation: Nexus 9000 switches, including the 9504 and 9508, do not support multiple VDCs, and every resource lives in the default VDC. Keeping vdc_id, and the later note about 'vdc_id nuances' on modular systems, carries over a Nexus 7000 concept that does not apply to this platform.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the vdc_id guidance for the Nexus 9500. If per-supervisor attribution matters, key on module or supervisor slot instead.

findings.explanation: CoPP class counters and COPP_DROPS syslog report per-class policer drops on the switch's control plane. They are not flow or session records (Network_Traffic), and they are not host CPU, memory or storage metrics (Performance). The schema text hedges this with 'control-plane destined traffic proxies' and 'cpu-adjacent policing', which signals that the fit is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to none, or state plainly that no CIM datamodel fits CoPP counters and the UC runs on raw sourcetypes. Rewrite schema and dataModelAcceleration to match.

findings.explanation: The subcategory grounding lists Nexus data as cisco:nexus:syslog, cisco:nexus:nxapi and cisco:nexus:netconf, and NDI data as cisco:ndi:anomaly and cisco:ndi:syslog. The UC uses different sourcetype names (cisco:nxos:*, cisco:ndi:health) without explaining where they come from, so the UC and its guide disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the sourcetypes with the ones the chosen collection app actually emits (check the 7777 app's props.conf), and update docs/guides/datacenter-fabric-sdn.md or the UC so the two match. Note that the guide also lists Splunkbase 6876 for the Nexus TA, but the cached catalog shows 6876 is the 'Network Monitoring App'.

findings.explanation: COPP-5-COPP_DROPS5 is real, but the number tracks the configured logging level (COPP_DROPSn), and the threshold is a dropped-byte count. I could not confirm a COPP-2-COPP_LIST mnemonic, the NX-API DN sys/copp/inst/proto-{class}, an NDI /sedgeapi/v1/site_health endpoint, or a 'Cisco-NX-OS-device-yang/copp-state' gNMI path. They look invented.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the NX-OS system message guide for COPP mnemonics, the NX-API DME model reference for the CoPP MO and stats DNs, the NDI API reference for site health, and the Cisco-NX-OS-device YANG tree for the CoPP container (System/copp-items). Remove any path that cannot be confirmed. Note that COPP_DROPSn is only emitted when `logging drop threshold <bytes> level n` is configured.

findings.explanation: The implementation never says that drop syslog only appears after `logging drop threshold` is configured per class. Without that step the syslog lane is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a prerequisite step: configure `logging drop threshold <bytes> level 5` under each monitored class in a custom copp-system-p-policy copy.

findings.explanation: The primary reference, 'NX-OS Security Configuration Guide — Control Plane Policing', points at the cisco.com home page instead of the CoPP chapter. The openVuln PSIRT API reference is unrelated to CoPP drop detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the Nexus 9000 'Configure Control Plane Policing' chapter and the Cisco 'Verify Control Plane Policing Violations on Nexus Platforms' tech note. Drop the PSIRT reference.

findings.explanation: None of the scenarios names a real cause of benign CoPP drops. Real causes include routing reconvergence after a link flap, ARP or ND bursts during VM migration, SNMP or NX-API polling hitting the management/monitoring class, multicast join storms, or ISSU or reload recovery. 'Scheduled automation elevates fabric_token' is not meaningful.
findings.quote: **Batch `sum` on `cisco:nxos:syslog`** — Scheduled automation elevates `fabric_token` without crossing `class_baseline_global` > 25
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the scenarios with CoPP-specific benign drivers (reconvergence, ARP/ND bursts after mobility events, monitoring-class drops from aggressive pollers, post-reload adjacency rebuild) and say how to tell each one apart.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, but the reviewer is an agent and the content contains platform errors (Nexus 7000 naming, VDCs on the 9500, a deprecated add-on). There is no sign of SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until a human SME validates the UC against a Nexus 9000 lab.

findings.explanation: The detection fires on spikes relative to a per-class average, not on sustained duration. The explanation also leaves out that attack-like bursts (ARP, BGP) are called out separately.
findings.quote: When those governors discard traffic too long, we warn your crews early
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the check warns when a switch's built-in protection throws away much more management traffic than usual, which can mean a storm, a misbehaving device, or an attack.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: dropped_pkts_5min is coalesced to 0, so `isnotnull(dropped_pkts_5min)` is always true and the `where` clause passes every event, including non-CoPP syslog. policy_name defaults to the literal 'copp-system-policy-strict', which is a Nexus 7000-style name, so missing data looks like 'expected_bundle' and real Nexus 9000 names (copp-system-p-policy-*) fall into 'vendor_named_custom'.

The SPL sums NX-API policer counters, which are typically cumulative, per 5-minute bin without computing deltas, so dropped_pkts_5min grows with poll count. sigma_proxy is a ratio to the mean, not a standard-deviation score, so the '3-sigma' wording in the prose is false. The search never filters to alertable rows: `head 420` returns steady_watch rows too.

T1592 (Gather Victim Host Information) is a pre-compromise reconnaissance technique that defenders seldom observe. An LLDP/CDP surge hitting CoPP does not evidence it. T1499.004 (Application or System Exploitation DoS) is also a loose fit for control-plane flooding; consider T1498 or T1499 at the parent level.

summary: The CoPP topic is well chosen, but the text names a deprecated Cisco add-on under the wrong name, uses Nexus 7000 CoPP policy and class names on a Nexus 9000 UC, refers to a 'default' CoPP profile that does not exist, puts VDC handling on 9500 chassis that cannot run multiple VDCs, and maps the signal to CIM models that do not fit. Several NX-API, gNMI and NDI paths read as invented.
